devices.title: Devices
devices.speaker: Audio output (speaker/headset)
devices.outputUnsupported: Choosing an audio output is not supported in this browser (only Chrome/Edge for now) - the app uses the system's default speaker/headset.
devices.hint: If the chosen device is no longer available when a call starts, the system default is used automatically. Switching microphone/webcam during a call applies immediately; otherwise, it takes effect the next time you join voice/turn on the camera. The audio output always changes immediately.

cameraAsk.label: Ask when turning on the camera
cameraAsk.hint: Opens a preview to choose the webcam and background

autoplay.title: Media autoplay
autoplay.description: Decides whether OTHER participants' webcam/screen plays on its own when they turn it on, or waits for you to click "Watch". Never affects audio (mic) and never YOUR own media - only what you watch from others.
autoplay.hint: Hiding someone's media specifically, or muting their audio just for you, is in the ⋮ menu of the participant list or directly on their tile during the call.

noiseSuppression.title: Noise suppression
noiseSuppression.hint: Only reduces noise on YOUR microphone - does not affect what you hear from others. Changing the mode takes effect the next time you join a voice channel.
noiseSuppression.rnnoiseHint: RNNoise (open source, xiph/rnnoise) runs in your browser via WASM - handles background noise (keyboard, chatter, fan) better than the native suppressor; a low level keeps more of the original audio, a high level prioritizes cutting noise.
noiseSuppression.gtcrnHint: GTCRN (open source) also runs via WASM, with a newer network than RNNoise - better suppression quality on standard benchmarks, still light enough for real time; a low level keeps more of the original audio, a high level prioritizes cutting noise.
noiseSuppression.deepfilternetHint: DeepFilterNet3 (open source, Rikorose/DeepFilterNet) is the strongest and heaviest model on the list - it cuts ~20dB of background noise while barely touching speech in our tests, but downloads ~24MB of assets (self-hosted) the first time you join voice with this mode, and uses more CPU than the others. Here the level is the model's attenuation limit: 0% leaves the audio untouched, 100% allows the maximum cut.

micGate.label: Microphone sensitivity
micGate.hint: Cuts anything below the threshold - silence/background noise is no longer sent
micGate.help: Click "Test microphone" to see your level live (red line = chosen threshold) and calibrate before enabling. It runs AFTER the noise suppression above, on the same outgoing track - it changes what leaves your microphone, not what you hear. Changing the threshold (or turning it on/off) only takes effect the next time you join a voice channel.

pushToTalk.label: Push-to-talk
pushToTalk.hint: Mic only transmits while the key below is held down
pushToTalk.noKeyWarning: With no key assigned, the mic stays muted in voice channels - assign one before leaving.
pushToTalk.help: While enabled, the mic starts muted in any voice channel and only transmits while the key is held. Manual mute still works on top, even while holding the key.
pushToTalk.globalHint: In the desktop app the key works even when the window is unfocused/minimized.
